title: Three-point density correlations in a weakly interacting 2D Fermi liquid
abstract: We study the three-point equal-time correlations of the density in a weakly interacting spin 1/2 Fermi gas and present two new results. First, we compute the three-point correlation for the total density $ρ= ρ_\uparrow + ρ_\downarrow$ exactly as a function of momentum to first order in a dimensionless interaction parameter ${\cal I}$. This generalizes a previous result that related the three-point function to the Landau Fermi liquid parameters $F_0^s$ and $F_0^a$ and applied in a certain long-wavelength collinear limit. Second, we compute the leading order ${\cal O}({\cal I}^3)$ interaction correction to the same-spin three-point correlation function in the long-wavelength collinear limit. These results are directly relevant to current experiments on atomic Fermi gases using quantum gas microscopy.
summary: This paper theoretically calculates the three-point density correlations in a weakly interacting 2D Fermi liquid. Using perturbative methods, it derives interaction corrections for both total and same-spin density correlators. The results are highly relevant for interpreting upcoming experimental measurements using quantum gas microscopy on atomic Fermi gases.
main_problem: The study focuses on calculating the three-point equal-time density correlations ($ho^3$) in a weakly interacting two-dimensional Fermi liquid.
main_result: The authors derive explicit, perturbative results for both the total and same-spin density three-point correlators, providing corrections beyond the standard long-wavelength collinear limit.
method: The calculations employ a systematic perturbative expansion in the interaction parameter ($I$) using diagrammatic techniques (Feynman diagrams) within the framework of Fermi liquid theory.
model_or_system: The system is modeled as a spin 1/2 Fermi gas confined to two dimensions, interacting via an attractive contact potential. The analysis uses Hamiltonian formulations and correlation functions derived from quantum field theory methods.
key_observables: Total density three-point correlator ($s_{ho}^3(q_1, q_2)$) and same-spin three-point correlator ($s_{\uparrow}^3(q_1, q_2)$).
important_parameters: The dimensionless interaction parameter $I = -1/\log k_F a$, the Fermi momentum $k_F$, and various wave vectors ($\mathbf{q}_i$). The Long-Wavelength Collinear (LWC) limit is a key regime analyzed.
main_assumptions: The theory relies on perturbative expansions in weak interactions ($N_0|u| \ll 1$) and assumes the validity of Fermi liquid theory, although results are extended beyond its strict limits.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate Feynman diagrams for correlation functions at different orders, compare exact calculations against asymptotic approximations and standard Fermi liquid predictions across various momentum configurations (e.g., isosceles triangles).
paper_structure: The paper proceeds by defining the observables, calculating the zeroth-order non-interacting case, and then systematically deriving the first-order interaction corrections ($L_1$ or $s^{(1)}$) through complex integral evaluations in momentum space.
why_interesting: This work provides highly detailed theoretical predictions for correlation functions in ultracold atomic Fermi gases, directly connecting fundamental many-body theory (Fermi liquid parameters) to measurable quantities accessible via quantum gas microscopy.
